facts.site: Marrindal Concentrator and Hydrocarbon Transfer Facility
facts.title: residual pressure found after isolation of TK-4210

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was first aid or minor property damage. The potential outcome was rated 2 against the site's consequence scale, above the 1 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control HYDROCARBON_TRANSFER_CONTROL: the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels had been bypassed, and the accident investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.

recommendations: Confirm at the next spot check that the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels on TK-4210 performs as designed.
response.sequence: Work was under way in maintaining sealing systems on rotating equipment, specifically replacing seals and seal support fluid. TK-4210 (hydrocarbon day tanks and surge vessel) is in service for diesel and light hydrocarbon day storage, discharge surge suppression. The task proceeded during an intrusive maintenance task while the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels had been bypassed. The pressure energy involved is held as hydraulic accumulator, and the recorded presentation was jet release, stored-energy discharge, rupture.
response.summary: On 7 September 2006 a near hit was recorded on TK-4210 at Marrindal Concentrator and Hydrocarbon Transfer Facility during an intrusive maintenance task; pressure energy held as hydraulic accumulator was not released.
